name: Air
summary: Air is the mixture of gases around the Earth. Dry air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.93% argon and 0.04% carbon dioxide, with traces of neon, helium, methane and others, and it holds up to about 4% water vapour as well, depending on the weather. Of all of it the body uses only the oxygen: a resting adult breathes 6 to 8 litres a minute, keeps about a quarter of the oxygen in each breath and breathes out a little carbon dioxide in its place.
advisory: Any gas breathed in place of air leaves less oxygen in each breath: nitrous from a balloon, helium, butane, aerosols or solvents. Breathe air between hits, never with a bag over the head or a mask over the face, and get anyone who faints out to fresh air at once. Canned “compressed air” for dusting keyboards isn’t air: it’s a liquefied gas such as difluoroethane, and breathing it in can stop the heart, even the first time.

warnings.text: Up a mountain the air is still 21% oxygen, but thinner: at 2,500 m each breath carries about a quarter less of it, and at 5,500 m half. Above about 2,500 m altitude sickness can start, with a headache, nausea and poor sleep, and going higher with it can lead to fluid on the lungs or the brain. Climb slowly, skip alcohol and sleeping pills up there, and go down if it gets worse.

Carbon monoxide, from a faulty boiler or heater, a car engine, or a barbecue or charcoal burning indoors, has no colour or smell and can kill in a closed room. A headache, dizziness and nausea that ease outside are the sign: get out into fresh air and call for help.
